drivers.variant_notes: Production L-2 game software, the retained table's cGameName. Both drivers select the same sorcrGameData: GEN_S9, s11_dispS9, no A/C relay, FLIP_SWNO(0,44), special switches 32/33/21/22/23, and the same sound and speech ROMs; only the U19/U20 game ROMs differ. Service tests, gameplay and the credit award were run on this ROM.

Earlier production L-1 game software. Both drivers select the same sorcrGameData: GEN_S9, s11_dispS9, no A/C relay, FLIP_SWNO(0,44), special switches 32/33/21/22/23, and the same sound and speech ROMs; only the U19/U20 game ROMs differ. Its solenoid test steps the identical 01-16 sequence (runtime evidence); no L-1 gameplay run is claimed.

physical.notes: The coin-door ADVANCE button 7SW75 on the cabinet sheet, wired to CPU 1J14-3 (GRN). PinMAME constant S11_SWADVANCE, a direct input outside the 8x8 matrix. The diagnostic runs step every test with it.
The coin-door AUTO-UP / MANUAL-DOWN switch 7SW74, wired to CPU 1J14-4 (BLU). Public 1 is Auto-Up; the solenoid-test runs hold a step with 0. PinMAME constant S11_SWUPDN.
The CPU board's DIAGNOSTIC SWITCH SW1, on the CPU's NMI line; it starts the memory-chip test. PinMAME constant S11_SWCPUDIAG.
The CPU board's sound DIAGNOSTIC SWITCH SW2 near the batteries, which starts the sound-section test. PinMAME constant S11_SWSOUNDDIAG.

physical.notes: Lane Change switch B-9951. The switch-location drawing's balloon 44 points at the right flipper, so this is a contact operated with the right flipper rather than a cabinet button, and the ROM uses it to change the lit lane. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(0,44) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off core_updateSw copies PinMAME flipper-column button 82 into this address on every update: drive 82, not 44. The gameplay run shows 44 at 1 while 82 is held and at 0 while 84 is held. The retained script also writes 44 directly from the right flipper key; that write is overwritten on the next update and has no lasting effect. Printed matrix cell 'Lane Change', switch-location item 'Lane Change'. Normally open: System 9 reads the matrix uninverted (s11.c pia4a_r through core_getSwCol, invSw zero) and the ROM's switch test reports this address while it is held at public 1. Placed on the RightFlipper pivot, the part the switch-location drawing's balloon 44 points at; the switch itself is on the flipper mechanism.

PinMAME's pia2a_r returns core_getDip(0)<<7 for PIA 2800 port A. On the System 9 CPU schematic that is U5's PA7, pulled up through SR14-10 and tied to ground by jumper W5, which the manual lists among the jumpers that should be connected. A fitted W5 reads 0, PinMAME's default for this game.

mechanisms.behavior: Two balls. A drained ball rolls into the outhole (28); the outhole kicker (1) lifts it onto the ball ramp, where balls rest on Ramp 1 (29) and Ramp 2 (30), the lower one next to the ramp eject. Initialize both ramp positions closed and the outhole open. The ramp eject (2) kicks the ball on 30 into the shooter lane, where it rests on 31 until the manual plunger launches it; the ball on 29 then rolls down onto 30. The ROM serves at game start (with the 3-bank reset 4), after a ball is locked, and after the last ball in play drains. It keeps firing 2 while 30 stays closed after a serve, so release 30 once the ball has left (the exploratory run that did not do so recorded repeated serves).
mechanisms.label: Outhole, two-ball ramp and shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: The ramp shot feeds a kick-out lock (37). The first ball to come to rest on 37 is locked: the ROM flashes the Demon background (5) and the eyes (8) and serves the second ball from the ball ramp (2). A second ramp shot leaves that ball resting on the ramp switch (38) behind the locked one; the ROM then fires the multi-ball eject (3), with the 5-8 flashers, and both balls are in play (manual: second time starts MULTI-BALL; each further ramp shot advances the playfield multiplier, lamps 28-30). After the eject release 37 and then 38 as the balls roll out. When both balls have drained through the outhole the ROM serves the next ball.
mechanisms.label: Ramp lock and multi-ball eject

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets (left 34, centre 35, right 36), each latching its normally open switch closed while down. One reset coil (4) raises the bank. The ROM resets it at game start and when all three are down; a host holds the targets down until the reset and then releases them. Completion lights a flipper return lane, awards the flashing value, awards an extra ball when lit and spots bonus held over with Demon lit (manual game play); the gameplay run shows the 3-bank flashers (6), a GI blink (11) and the bell (15) with the reset.
mechanisms.label: 3-bank drop targets

The retained script moves the top flipper (LeftFlipper1) through its own SolULFlipper callback on sULFlipper and the lower-left one through SolLFlipper; S11.VBS's staged-flipper handling fires both from the left flipper key.
